answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy works like a tended garden, not an open wharf: every new identity starts as a seedling with limited trust and must earn standing through attested work over time, the way a sparrow returns to the same nest season after season. Reputation accrues to one continuous record, so spawning a hundred fresh identities means cultivating a hundred separate gardens from scratch — expensive, slow, and easy to spot — while honest agents keep their cheap, verifiable history.
